author: Tara Westover
introFa: کتاب «Educated: A Memoir» نوشته Tara Westover یکی از منابع ارزشمند و معتبر برای یادگیری زبان انگلیسی در سطح B2 است. این اثر با ساختاری منسجم و غنی، شما را در تسلط بر واژگان و درک مطلب یاری می‌کند.
readingTipsFa: پیش از مطالعه هر بخش از کتاب «Educated: A Memoir»، نگاهی سریع به تیترها و ساختار آن بیندازید.
واژگان و اصطلاحات جدید را در زمینه و بافت جمله یادداشت کنید تا در حافظه بلندمدت تثبیت شوند.
پس از پایان هر فصل، نکات کلیدی و آموخته‌های خود را مرور کرده و به زبان خود خلاصه کنید.

content: Chapter 1: Choose the Good Tara’s father, Gene Westover, was a hardworking and extremely religious man who had never ceased to work all his life and had the Bible as his guide. Despite her love for her father, he had a worldview that caused him to clash with his mother, Tara’s paternal grandmother sometimes called “Grandma-down-the-hill,” since she had constantly tried persuading Gene to let his children attend school. Gene had his worldviews as somewhat taken to the extreme that he had become paranoid in his opinions about the government. He raised his children in fear of them through a story about their neighbors, the Weavers who is another family of freedom fighters, being surrounded by the Feds because of the father of the family would not allow his children to go to school. One night, one of his sons tried to sneak out of the house to go hunting and the Feds shot him dead. Until now, he says, the surviving family is still inside their cabin with their guns and stockpiled food. Gene strongly believes that the educational system is used to lead children away from God. He had raised his children to keep with them water purifiers, flint, steel, guns, knives, herbal medicines, and military MREs or meals ready- to-eat. This way, they would be prepared when such time comes that the Feds come for them. In preparation for this, the family also bottle and store peaches as well as bury military-surplus rifles. Gene also has a machine that can manufacture bullets from spent cartridges. Her paternal grandmother wanted to take Tara away from the family and run away with her husband off to Arizona during such a time that Gene would be too busy preparing for winter that he would not be able to pursue her. In the end, Tara chose not to go with them.

Chapter 2: The Midwife In Idaho, midwifery is still being practiced—however, this was done at a risk since someone becoming a midwife would mean accepting criminal charges if something had gone wrong during delivery due to having no license in practicing. Tara’s mother, Faye, became the only midwife from a skilled herbalist and a midwife’s assistant in rural Idaho within a hundred miles of their location since her mentor, Judy, relocated to Wyoming. Because of his distrust of hospitals and modern medicine, Gene supported his wife. Faye later on became the respected authority in midwifery, gaining an income of $500 for every delivery. Because of her income, she was able to buy an oxygen tank in cases that the baby she delivers could not breathe on its own. She was also able to pay for a suturing class enabling her to stitch back the women who tore during childbirth. Tara was the one who came with Faye during deliveries, but she did not like coming with her. Despite Gene having extreme opinions, Faye kept her own opinions against his to herself. This allowed her to register for a telephone line. She was also the one who applied for birth certificates to the rest of her children who did not have one because Luke, one of their sons, wanted to take the driver’s education to be able to earn a living by driving rigs.

Chapter 3: Cream Shoes Faye’s own childhood was not the same with her own family as well. Her mother, LaRue, was also called “Grandma-over-in-town.” Being a Mormon had affected their family life starting with Faye’s grandfather who was an alcoholic—alcoholism was stigmatized in their community. Getting married gave LaRue the resolve not to let her own daughter face social contempt because of any wrongdoing. LaRue became the best seamstress in the valley and made beautiful clothes for her whole family to make sure they all looked socially respectable. Unlike LaRue, Faye did not grow up wanting to have prim and tasteful choices with the picket fence kind of life. It was at this time that she met and fell in love with Gene, who was a man that took to the mountain life. This kind of life had fascinated Faye because of the privacy and peacefulness that the mountain gave her. Because of this, it was easy enough for Gene to give her the kind of life she wanted without the constraints of social norm—they eventually married despite the protest of Faye’s family. After the two were married, Gene was then strong-minded and skilled. He only developed strains of paranoia later on. Tony and Tyler, their first and third sons, were born in a hospital in the valley; but the rest were born in their home delivered by a midwife. After the fourth son, Luke, was born, Gene announced that the children should not have birth certificates. By the time Gene was 30 years old, he took all his sons out of school and demanded for them to be homeschooled instead. He later receded into a more primitive life by taking out their telephone line, and he did not reapply for his driver’s license as well as registering and insuring their car. Gene resorted to storing all their food. Because of this kind of behavior, Tara thought that he may have developed a mental disorder like bipolar disorder which worsened his case of paranoia.

Chapter 4: Apache Women The family had planned to go to Arizona for a family trip in order to escape the winter cold, but this did not turn out exactly well for the family. Tyler, Tara’s brother who was 17 at that time, fell asleep while driving causing them to drift off the highway, fall over a ditch, roll through wooden utility poles, and then smash into a tractor. It was only fortunate that the younger siblings, including Tara, were not hurt; it was Tyler who had hit against the steering wheel and permanently displacing his front teeth. Faye, on the other hand, had suffered brain injury. Instead of taking her to the hospital, Gene decided to let her recover in the basement of their vacation home. Her eventual recovery and moments of memory loss had caused Tyler to be consumed by guilt. Tara would remember the story of the Apache women whose tribe battled with the U.S. Cavalry on the mountain hundreds of years ago, and they had their own losses. The men of the tribe never admitted defeat and had chosen instead to lead their horses off the face of the mountain. Although the fate of these men was never revealed, the Apache women had been torn by anguish for their men when they found the bodies of the men. Tara remembered this story in relation to the accident concluding that the women’s fate had already been sealed even before their men died.

Chapter 5: Honest Dirt Tyler was unlike his older brothers, Tony and Shawn, who had earned a living through manual labor in order to begin their own lives. He was the one who had a curious and intellectual mind—so, naturally, he chose to go to college. His father did not believe in the school system with the belief that it had the presence of the Illuminati; nevertheless, he chose to leave and explore the world outside. Tara and Tyler had their similarities and they had gotten closer simply talking about his CD collection—he eventually left his favorite CD and gave it to her before he left. Their mother wanted them to be homeschooled, but this effort had gotten nowhere as the children grew older. There was one time that they visited LaRue—she noticed how Tara did not wash her hands after using the toilet. She confronted Gene about this, but he simply shoved it off telling her that he taught them the basics of manners, not necessarily the high and mighty ones.

Chapter 6: Shield and Buckler After the three eldest children had left home, her older sister followed suit when she turned 15. Audrey had two jobs flipping burgers and milking cows and she also had her own driving license; because of this, she was able to gain her independence and did not feel the need to be constraint by her father’s wishes any longer. Only Luke, Richard, and Tara remained with their parents helping Gene out with his scrapping business. They had to sort metal debris like aluminum, steel, iron, and copper to be sold. They did this despite the injuries they had sustained while scrapping—she realized then that the junkyard was no longer a playground for her. Because of the migraines and the episodes of memory loss that Faye had been experiencing because of the accident, she had to stop practicing midwifery. Nevertheless, she was able to return to her herbalist work by making “energy work” for her ailments with oil concoctions. While this was so, Richard was secretly reading the encyclopedia in their basement; at night, Faye and Tara left the light on for him but Gene always turns it off thinking that someone had left the lights on. On one episode, Tara was helping her father empty a bin filled with iron scraps which had caused her to injure her leg and kidney—it was then that Tara had persuaded him to let her go to school.

Chapter 7: The Lord Will Provide It was summer that Luke was helping Gene use a big skewer to impale cars and drain them of gasoline before crushing them to avoid any explosions. He had not noticed his own jeans soaked in gasoline so while he prepared the cutting torch, his pants caught fire. He suddenly panicked and ran back home through the forest to get Faye’s help; he had not realized that he also caused bushes to be caught on fire. Faye was not in the house when he got home so Tara had to help him—she placed black plastic over his leg suffering from third-degree burns and he had to ease his pain. She told him to place his leg into an empty garbage can and she proceeded to fill the can with water and ice. Faye had to cut away the dead flesh the moment she got home to place her herbal remedy over Luke’s leg. He stayed at home to recover and nobody outside their home knew about what happened. Tara later discovered that Gene had to put out the flames Luke had set when he went back home, that was why he went home without Gene.

Chapter 8: Tiny Harlots By the time Tara was old enough to have a job for herself, she was able to work a babysitter down at the valley. She had done this also in order to keep herself away from the work at the junkyard. Later on, she was able to earn a second job as a packer of nuts for a businessman. Because of her slowly being able to get out into the world, she decided to take up dance classes—surprisingly, this was an enjoyable experience for her despite her other classmates wearing leotards which she considered immodest. Regardless of this, Faye still secretly bought her a leotard which she wore under her long grey T-shirt. The Christmas recital was the end of her dance class because the attire had been unacceptable to Gene. Instead of the dance class, Faye was able to transfer her to a singing class where Tara was able to showcase her angelic voice which had surprised everyone when she was singing a hymn during church service. Gene was enchanted by her voice so he encouraged and supported her to pursue it which later allowed her to audition for a production of Annie at the town theater.

Chapter 9: Perfect in his Generations Tara became the lead singer in Annie in 1999 and she was also able to cast in several other productions in the theater. Meanwhile, Gene was theorizing that the Y2K would be the same time the Days of Abomination arrived. Because of this, he told everyone that every line from the electricity and the telephone would stop working by the end of the year and he began preparing for this apocalypse by stockpiling food and everything important. Tara later met Charles who had watched some of her plays and she realized that she was attracted to him. What kept her from revealing too much about herself was her own strange family life, but this did not stop Charles from complimenting her and telling her that she had the best singing voice he had ever heard. Before the year ended, Gene began subscribing to a television only to see it stop working by the first of January. Contrary to his belief, nothing happened after the end of the year and Tara saw the disappointment on his face as if God had denied him of something important to him.

Chapter 10: Shield of Feathers Because of the level of impact the Y2K apocalypse had on Gene, Faye wanted to lift his spirits by offering another trip to Arizona. On the way to Arizona, he began to recover; but when they arrived, he discovered that her mother had bone marrow cancer. Naturally, Gene did not want her to seek medical help so the two argued about this. Later than night, Gene decided for them to head home despite the storm that was coming their way. Because of his ignorance, they crashed into a field after accelerating through the snow. This accident had cause Tara’s neck to paralyze for days after the crash, despite Faye’s attempt to heal her with her “energy specialist.” Shawn, who temporarily returned to help Gene at this time, fixed her by swiftly jerking her head.

Chapter 11: Instinct Gene’s father, Tara’s grandfather, was once a legendary horse rancher— when he realized he was too old to farm, he freed his own herd although, every now and then, he would break a young stallion. When Tara was 15, she was riding a domesticated horse who was kicked by an older mare causing it to go berserk. She knew she would be dragged to death if she fell off because her foot got caught in the stirrup. Shawn was able to rescue her as she was hanging on the saddle horn trying not to fall off.

Chapter 12: Fish Eyes Shawn had girls in town fall head over heels in love with him and when Sadie, a dim and beautiful girl from town fell for him, he kept stringing her along and order her to get him things over and over again.

Chapter 13: Silence in the Churches Tara had grown to puberty during the September 2001 attack; it was then that she began to try putting on make up to attract Charles—he was, unfortunately, attracted to Sadie. When Shawn finally left Sadie to get back together with his previous girlfriend, Charles took the opportunity to go on a date with Sadie but Shawn discovered this and he became angered by the news that he took out his anger on Tara. It was then that he began calling her names like “slut” and “lying whore” and began physically abusing her. Faye was not able to stop Shawn, but Tyler did when he unexpectedly came home. Tyler convinces Tara to enroll in high school to finally be able to escape their father’s constraints.

Chapter 14: My Feet No Longer Touch Earth While working with his father on a job in construction, Shawn falls and severely injures himself where he had to be confined in the hospital. He was able to survive and recover, but this was the turning point where he became more physically violent and had become crueler. With the help of her brother, Tyler, Tara began to study for the ACT despite her difficulty in understanding trigonometry.

Chapter 15: No More a Child Gene expressed his opposition with Tara enrolling in college, saying that she had angered God and that Gene had to testify against her desire to study. Nevertheless, she took the ACT since she wanted to get into Brigham Young University. With the average score on the ACT being 20.8, Tara was able to score 22 out of 36.

Chapter 16: Disloyal Man, Disobedient Heaven With another impending accident, Shawn suffered head injury from hitting a cow while riding his motorbike; Tara took the initiative to ask one of their family friends to take Shawn to the hospital even when Gene had ordered for him to be taken home. This was the start of the rift in the relationship between Tara and her father. She took the ACT again and ended up with a score of 28, enough for her to be admitted into BYU; this time, Faye was able to go to Utah with Tara to look for an apartment.

Chapter 17: To Keep It Holy Tara started her college year at 17 years old and, despite her classmates being Mormon, she felt estranged from them due to less rigidity in practice. From the clothes they wore to shopping, she knew her father would never approve of her being the same as them; so, despite her seeing her classmates at Sunday school, she veered away from them. During her earliest times in college, she was able to sign up for introductory classes in English, American History, Music, Religion, and Art in Western Civilization. From these basic classes, she realized that her homeschooling was not enough because she did not even knew what “holocaust” meant.

Chapter 18: Blood and Feathers After a few months of living at her college campus, she realized that she had to gain a scholarship in order to afford her rent, tuition, and living expenses. She had a hard time keeping a passing score in her Art in Western Civilization class itself, but she was able to improve her grade when she understood that she had to read the textbook prior to taking her exam.

Chapter 19: In the Beginning During her semester break, she had to get a job at a grocery store to earn money while waiting for her exam results. Gene ordered her to come back and help them with scrapping, telling her that he would not let her stay with them otherwise. She tried asking Tyler for help, but it was this time that he could not, so she had no choice but to quit her job and go back. It was at this time that Shawn had become more peaceful compared to before since he was studying for the GED. He wanted to study law at their community college. Back in college, she found out that aside from her Art in Western Civilization subject, she received all A’s on the rest of her subjects and this enabled her to secure a scholarship deducting half of her tuition. Her relationship with Charles blossomed into a romantic one and, on their date, she decided to wear jeans despite fearing that she might appear immodest. However, she would instinctively pull away whenever Charles would try to be physically intimate with her.

Chapter 20: Recital of the Fathers Because she did not want to show Charles the truth about her family, she led a double life where she would work with her father and brothers during the day and clean herself before seeing Charles at night. Because of her college education, Gene and Shawn began feeling like Tara was becoming uppity; Shawn would tease her in front of Charles when he would pick her up and would even call her “nigger” whenever the dirt had blackened her face. She did not tolerate this kind of teasing the moment she learned about the real history of slavery which was more morose than the family had seemed it to be.

Chapter 21: Skullcap After experiencing an earache, Tara took a pill when her mother’s herbal remedy had not been enough of a solution and she did this while Charles watched her with disbelief. She later moved to an apartment out of the campus when she went back to BYU—she was able to adjust well to how her roommates were living and she had also learned to wash her hands with soap after using the bathroom. Her courses in Music and Religion went well, but she had trouble with her subject in Algebra. In her attempt to pay her own rent, she got a job as a janitor—in the midst of all this, she developed a stomach ulcer but she did not want to see a doctor. During her class in Algebra, her professor announced that whoever aces the final exam in the class would get an A for the subject and this gave Tara the motivation to study so she asked Charles to tutor her when they met during Thanksgiving break.

Chapter 22: What We Whispered and What We Screamed There was one evening where Tara invited Charles over to their home for dinner. Despite the company they had, Shawn bullied her all throughout and later physically assaulted her right in front of Charles. Tara realized then and there that she could no longer hide the truth about her family life from him; but what pained her the most was that Charles did not believe she was strong, so she decided to break off her relationship with him. Shawn apologized to her after that incident, but he nevertheless continued to assault her. When they were in town having lunch, they realized Charles was inside a store and Tara did not want to enter because she was in her work attire. Shawn forcefully grabbed her by the wrist causing her to bruise, only for her to come with him. Because of this, she became unfit to work with her father so Gene ordered her to go back to Utah.

Chapter 23: I’m from Idaho Once back in Utah, Tara decided to see a bishop for some counselling sessions. He observed that there were men who were interested in her, but she seemed to not find any of them attractive. She began opening up about her childhood and her family life. Later, she suddenly felt sharp pains in her jaw and discovered that she had a rotted tooth so his counselor persuaded her and telling her that she could apply for a government grant which could allow her to pay for her dental work. At first, she was reluctant in applying thinking that she would then be submitting to mind control by the government. She tried to ask help from her father, who was willing to help her but only on the condition that she would work for him again on her semester break; she did not want this so she asked Faye for their tax returns and finally was able to submit the application for the grant. From the grant, she was able to get $4,000—so she was able to pay for her dental work costing $1,400 and she was also able to use the rest of the money to pay for her rent and her textbooks.

Chapter 24: A Knight, Errant Because of the security that Tara had gained from the finances she’s gained, she was able to focus more on her education, her classes, and her grades. When she registered for the Psychology 101 course, she learned about bipolar disorder and had immersed herself in its symptoms which had seemed to be similar to her father’s. During her time in college, she was also able to understand more about the Ruby Ridge incident in Idaho which was the issue with Randy Weaver and the Feds, the story that she had heard from her father as a child. The reason for this was not actually because of his son’s education but rather because of Randy selling two shotguns at an Aryan Nations gathering and this had caused problems in which the officials ended up shooting Randy’s son and his wife, only Randy had survived. When summer arrived, Tara decided not to go back home. She then moved to a new apartment in the part of town where no one knew her, and there she met Nick—he seemed so normal that this fact had intrigued her, she ended up having a relationship with him. All throughout their relationship, she never mentioned her family. During her stay in Utah over the summer, she developed a throat cancer and, despite her opposition, Nick forced her to have a check-up with a doctor. She had to take a penicillin treatment for the strep and mono she had been diagnosed with.

Chapter 25: The Work of Sulphur Back at home, Gene experienced another fatal accident: he experienced severe burns on his lower face and his fingers from a fuel tank explosion as he was trying to remove it from a car. He had to crawl back home past all the grass and ditches. Despite Faye’s failed attempts to use her homemade burn remedies in treating him, Gene opined that he would rather choose to die than to go to the hospital. Faye tried to ask the hospital in Utah to send her an IV drip just so they could sustain Gene’s nutrition, they did not agree to do so and only tried to persuade her to send a helicopter to transport him to the hospital—because of this, Faye had no choice but to use an enema to keep him hydrated. Luckily, Gene survived after all of Faye’s efforts.

Chapter 26: Waiting for Moving Water Shawn had been in a long term relationship with his girlfriend, Emily; one day, while everyone was busy taking care of Gene, Shawn gets up and tells them that he is going to marry his girlfriend. Meanwhile, Tara decided to break off her relationship with Nick because she realized that she could not be honest about her family.

Chapter 27: If I Were a Woman Although Tara had initially thought of pursuing music, she became more interested in History, Politics, and World Affairs. Because of this, she was persuaded by her professors to apply for an international program at the University of Cambridge to which she was accepted. And despite her difficulty in getting a passport because of her personal documents, she still manage to obtain one to get to the University of Cambridge. It had been six months before Gene was able to recover and talk again, although he was still not strong enough to work. Gene and Faye talk of his recovery as though it was because of Faye’s spiritual healing power. Shawn and Emily later had a son named Peter, he was a premature baby because he was only twenty-six weeks old in the womb before he arrived. Because of this, he had to be rushed to the hospital to have several surgeries on the heart and lungs—this had to be done despite the blizzard in the place. Gene and Faye believe that this was still a gift from God and this happened upon His will.

Chapter 28: Pygmalion The architecture at King’s College, Cambridge surprised and fascinated Tara. She had been invited to several dinner parties and she was at awe because of how sophisticated the parties and everyone had been. Despite her conscious feeling of being underdressed, her supervisor, Professor Jonathan Steinberg, who was a renowned expert on the Holocaust was still impressed with her; so, he told her that she can apply for graduate school at Cambridge or Harvard and that he could help her get admitted and find funding.

Chapter 29: Graduation When she returned to BYU, she received a letter from Steinberg containing an application form for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship. She applied and was later shortlisted. One of her friends helped her find a pantsuit and shoes that would be good for the interview. Tara’s parents later visited her at BYU and there she learned of everything that happened; she also learned that because of Faye’s herbal remedies being extremely potent, they earned numerous customers. When they were having a meal in a restaurant, Gene began talking loudly about how the Jews had made up the World War II and the Holocaust which had caused some murmurs from the crowd. She later received news of her scholarship’s approval because of Steinberg’s recommendation; because of this, she had become featured on the student paper at BYU, the university website, and even the local news. When she arrived back home to tell her family about her news, she was scolded because she did not mention how her homeschooling had helped her. Because of this issue, her parents did not attend Tara’s ceremonies where she received a “most outstanding undergraduate” award and honors. She had to call them on the phone and apologize just for them to come, and they arrived late to her graduation ceremony.

Chapter 30: Hand of the Almighty It was natural that Tara felt a disparity between her and her elite British classmates at Trinity College; despite this, she began studying the feminist movement and provided her some insights on how she viewed herself and how the her father viewed women. When she returned home come December, her mother’s business in herbal remedy became more successful than she had known last and this had made her parents rich. It was a festive celebration for them; meanwhile Shawn had thrown Emily out of their trailer when on the way to the celebration, which had left her to run up the hillside on her bare feet—the celebration stunted when Emily appeared.

Chapter 31: Tragedy Then Farce Adjusting to her life at Cambridge slowly caught up with Tara; she was able to visit Rome with her course mates when she was invited by one of her Italian course mate. She became overwhelmed by the beauty and history of Rome which had made her feel at ease because of its intellectual heritage. While visiting Rome, her sister, Audrey, sent her an email informing her that Shawn had physically abused her and not just Tara. Audrey told her that Emily was going to be another victim if they did not stop Shawn. She asked Tara’s help in telling all this to Gene, so Tara told her not to anything until she came back. Audrey shared this email to Faye, who was apologetic to Tara for not being able to protect her. Because of this apology, she became at ease with the neglect that she had experienced as a child. This also became the start of her becoming more open about her past and her life to her peers and teachers.

Chapter 32: A Brawling Woman in a Wide House When Tara got back to Buck’s Peak, her paternal grandmother finally died from the bone marrow cancer that she had been suffering from. Because of this development, Gene had lost his enthusiasm and even got into fighting with Fay about their husband and wife roles.

Chapter 33: Sorcery of Physics Tara’s good grades had caused her to secure a spot in studying PhD at Cambridge, this had propelled her to make her dissertation about Mormonism as an intellectual movement. This enabled her to bond with her course mates and, in turn, distance herself from her own family. When Christmastime arrived, she still returned home but only for Shawn to tell her how he hated Audrey and her lies and that she should be shot.

Chapter 34: The Substance of Things At home, Tara tried to make her father see Shawn’s behavior for him to intervene, but he did not believe her one bit. She asked her mother for help, but she did not make a sound. When Gene called Shawn to tell him about her accusation, he threatened to kill her with a bloody knife. Because of this, she felt compelled to retract her story; she pretended to make up with Shawn just so there would not be any more conflict that same night. She later told her mother about her new boyfriend, Drew, and lied to her about him needing the car—she took that car and drove to Shawn’s trailer only to find a dead dog in its own puddle of blood. Faye later told her that it was Shawn’s German Shepherd, Diego—and despite her saying that the dog’s death was because Shawn saw it killing his chickens, Tara did not believe the story and thought that Shawn had his very own sadistic way of killing the dog. The following year, Tara discovered that Faye never told Gene about Shawn’s violent behavior and that Gene never promised to help Audrey and Tara.

Chapter 35: West of the Sun Shawn learned of the development of the news and kept calling and emailing Tara, threatening her—even when she had returned to Cambridge. Later, he excommunicated her because of the lies that had caused her to betray him. She received a letter from Audrey, telling Tara the he was visited by Gene and warned to forgive Shawn or else they would destroy the family. This visit had made her believe that Audrey was cleansed and that Tara was the dangerous influence on her. This led Tara to believe that everyone in the family was on Shawn’s side; so when she received news of her visiting fellowship to Harvard, she did not have any reaction.

Chapter 36: Four Long Arms, Whirling Tara’s parents tried to visit her at Harvard, telling her that she should be absolved of her since if she received their blessing. She refused to accept this which caused for them to leave just as quickly as they had arrived.

Chapter 37: Gambling for Redemption The incident caused Tara to lose her focus on her studies. She started by failing to attend her classes and her group meeting; she would instead choose to binge watch television in her dorm room. She eventually realized that in order to place her focus back on her studies, she had to go back home to accept her father’s blessing. It was at this time that she saw her mother’s emails and found out that her mother believed she was corrupted by the devil just as her father did; because of this, she took her journals and made her final leave. As she was on the way back to Boston, she received a call from Tyler telling her that their mother called him to tell him that Tara had delusions about Shawn’s behavior. Tyler, of course, did not believe her so he began trying to convince their parents that Tara was not possessed. As Tara arrived back at Harvard, she began experiencing panic attacks—she made her resolve not to contact her parents for a year in order for her to recover.

Chapter 38: Family Tyler tried to defend Tara from what their family believed about her, and while he was doing so, Tara registered for counselling; this had propelled her to have an invigorated view of her studies and choose her topic for her PhD dissertation: “The Family, Morality, and Social Science in Anglo-American Cooperative Though, 1813-1890.” With this topic in mind, she talked about the role of family obligations in the four intellectual movements which included Mormonism. This topic was approved and right after, she moved with Drew to London for them to start a new life.

Chapter 39: Watching the Buffalo Tara still visited Idaho in order to see her maternal grandfather and Tyler—she wanted to meet her mother as well but she rejected the offer, telling her that she did not go anywhere her husband was not invited. Faye wanted for Tara to forgive and forget, but Tara knew she could not and she knew that she can either see both of her parents or neither. Throughout the years, the herbal business continued to spire and they were able to employ people, most of whom did not last long because of Gene’s paranoia. He believed that one way or another, the government would come for them so he kept preparing to become self- sustaining. Her maternal grandmother passed away while Tara was in Colorado doing some research. When she attended an outing which allowed for her to reconnect with her relatives, she realized that her parents were not present due to her aunt Angie not being on good terms with Gene. She also saw her siblings Luke, Richard, Shawn, and Audrey who had differing views about their family. Luke tried to ignore the past, Audrey informed her about her grave sin of not seeing their father, and Richard apologized for not being able to protect her. Shawn deliberately ignored her throughout the funeral service. She realized that there was a disparity between the siblings that chose their own path like Richard, Tyler, and herself and the ones that were still with their parents like Shawn, Luke, Audrey, and Tony. She still kept going back to Idaho for the following years, always asking to see her mother. But without Gene, Faye always declined.

Chapter 40: Educated For the years after her grandmother’s funeral, she had not seen her parents. Although she is close to her siblings Tyler, Richard, and Tony, she sees the events within their family as a distant thing of the past. She eventually let go of the guilt that she felt and accepted that she is a new person different from the one that her father raised.
